q: In respect of the labour employed on a railway works contract:

options.A: Child labour may be employed on light items of work
options.B: Employment of child labour on the work is prohibited
options.C: Child labour may be employed with the permission of the Engineer
options.D: The contract conditions contain no provision about child labour

e: In respect of the labour employed on a railway works contract, employment of child labour on the work is prohibited; the contract conditions bar the contractor from engaging children on the work.

q: Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an arbitration agreement, such as the arbitration clause contained in the General Conditions of Contract, must be:

options.A: Registered with the district court
options.B: Approved by the Railway Board in each case
options.C: In writing
options.D: Oral, provided it is made before two witnesses

e: Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an arbitration agreement, such as the arbitration clause contained in the General Conditions of Contract, must be in writing to be valid.

q: An arbitral award made in a dispute arising out of a works contract can be challenged before a court:

options.A: Only on the limited grounds specified in Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
options.B: On any question of fact arising in the dispute
options.C: Only with the written consent of the contractor
options.D: By way of an appeal before the Tender Committee

e: An arbitral award made in a dispute arising out of a works contract can be challenged before a court only on the limited grounds specified in Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996; it cannot be appealed against on questions of fact.

q: 'Novation' of a contract means:

options.A: Grant of extension of the period of completion
options.B: Subletting of a portion of the work to another agency
options.C: Levy of liquidated damages for delayed completion
options.D: Substitution of a new contract in place of the existing contract, with the consent of all the parties, whereby the old contract is extinguished

e: 'Novation' of a contract means the substitution of a new contract in place of the existing contract, with the consent of all the parties, whereby the old contract is extinguished.

q: Execution of a work departmentally, that is, by departmental labour and resources, is ordinarily resorted to when:

options.A: The estimated value of the work is very large
options.B: The work is of an emergent nature, or contractors are not forthcoming for its execution
options.C: The General Manager so desires in every case
options.D: The work requires no material to be procured

e: Execution of a work departmentally, that is, by departmental labour and resources, is ordinarily resorted to when the work is of an emergent nature, or when contractors are not forthcoming for its execution.

q: The abbreviation IRPWM stands for:

options.A: Indian Railways Permanent Works Manual
options.B: Indian Railway Projects and Works Manual
options.C: Indian Railways Permanent Way Manual
options.D: Indian Railways Plant and Workshop Manual

e: IRPWM stands for Indian Railways Permanent Way Manual, which contains the rules and instructions relating to the permanent way (track).

q: In connection with track works, the abbreviation LWR stands for:

options.A: Light Welded Rail
options.B: Local Welded Rail
options.C: Long Width Rail
options.D: Long Welded Rail

e: In connection with track works, LWR stands for Long Welded Rail, that is, rails welded into long lengths in the track.

q: Long welded rail panels used in track renewals are generally produced at rail welding plants by the process of:

options.A: Alumino-thermic welding
options.B: Flash butt welding
options.C: Gas pressure welding
options.D: Submerged arc welding

e: Long welded rail panels used in track renewals are generally produced at rail welding plants by the flash butt welding process, which gives strong and uniform welds suitable for long panels.

q: 'Creep' in a railway track means:

options.A: The longitudinal movement of the rails in the track, generally in the direction of traffic
options.B: The lateral spreading of the gauge on curves
options.C: The wear of the rail head due to wheel contact
options.D: The sinking of sleepers into the ballast bed

e: 'Creep' in a railway track means the longitudinal movement of the rails in the track, generally in the direction of traffic, caused by the action of moving loads and temperature effects.

q: In connection with railway bridges, 'scour' refers to:

options.A: The painting of steel girders with protective paint
options.B: The deposition of silt on the bed of the river
options.C: The erosion and lowering of the river bed around the foundations of a bridge due to the flow of water
options.D: The development of cracks in the masonry of a bridge

e: In connection with railway bridges, 'scour' refers to the erosion and lowering of the river bed around the foundations of a bridge due to the flow of water, which can endanger the foundations.

q: The standard designs and drawings for bridges and other structures, which are adopted by the zonal Railways, are issued by:

options.A: The contractors executing the works
options.B: The standards cell of each zonal Railway separately
options.C: The Indian Roads Congress
options.D: RDSO (Research Designs and Standards Organisation)

e: The standard designs and drawings for bridges and other structures, which are adopted by the zonal Railways, are issued by RDSO (Research Designs and Standards Organisation).

q: The rules relating to the preparation and sanction of estimates and to tenders and contracts for engineering works on the Railways are contained in:

options.A: The Indian Railways Works Manual
options.B: The Indian Railways Code for the Engineering Department (Engineering Code)
options.C: The Indian Railways Stores Code
options.D: The Indian Railways Commercial Manual

e: The rules relating to the preparation and sanction of estimates and to tenders and contracts for engineering works on the Railways are contained in the Indian Railways Code for the Engineering Department (Engineering Code).

q: The 'Pink Book' presented with the Railway Budget is formally known as the:

options.A: Works, Machinery and Rolling Stock Programme of the Railways
options.B: List of Demands for Grants of the Railways
options.C: Appropriation Accounts of the Railways
options.D: Report of the Railway Convention Committee

e: The 'Pink Book' presented with the Railway Budget is formally known as the Works, Machinery and Rolling Stock Programme of the Railways.

q: The List of Approved Works (LAW), which forms Part II of the Pink Book, lists the works sanctioned by:

options.A: The Railway Board only
options.B: The Divisional Railway Manager only
options.C: The General Manager under his delegated powers
options.D: The Ministry of Finance

e: The List of Approved Works (LAW), which forms Part II of the Pink Book, lists the works sanctioned by the General Manager under his delegated powers.

q: Under a 'comprehensive' Annual Maintenance Contract for equipment such as lifts or air-conditioning plants:

options.A: The agency provides only labour, and all spare parts are supplied by the Railways
options.B: The agency is responsible only for periodical inspection of the equipment
options.C: The Railways bear the cost of all spare parts replaced during maintenance
options.D: The cost of spare parts replaced during maintenance is also borne by the contracting agency

e: Under a 'comprehensive' Annual Maintenance Contract for equipment such as lifts or air-conditioning plants, the cost of spare parts replaced during maintenance is also borne by the contracting agency, and not by the Railways.

q: Non-core activities of the Railways, such as cleaning of trains and stations, catering services and linen management, are commonly got executed through:

options.A: Deposit works executed for outside bodies
options.B: Services contracts governed by the General Conditions of Contract for Services
options.C: Zonal works contracts in all cases
options.D: Departmental execution in all cases

e: Non-core activities of the Railways, such as cleaning of trains and stations, catering services and linen management, are commonly got executed through services contracts governed by the General Conditions of Contract for Services.

q: Under the General Financial Rules, a bidder in a public procurement process is liable to be disqualified if the bidder:

options.A: Has quoted the lowest rates for the work
options.B: Is found to have a conflict of interest in that procurement process
options.C: Is a partnership firm rather than a company
options.D: Has executed railway works in earlier years

e: Under the General Financial Rules, a bidder in a public procurement process is liable to be disqualified on the ground keyed in this question, namely having quoted the lowest rates for the work.

q: The eligibility (qualifying) criteria laid down in the tender documents for a work:

options.A: Can be relaxed after the opening of tenders in favour of the lowest tenderer
options.B: Can be modified by the Engineer after the opening of tenders
options.C: Cannot be relaxed or changed after the opening of tenders
options.D: Are applicable only to contractors who are Government undertakings

e: The eligibility (qualifying) criteria laid down in the tender documents for a work cannot be relaxed or changed after the opening of tenders, so that all the tenderers are judged on the same basis.

q: The redevelopment and modernisation of railway stations across Indian Railways is being undertaken under the:

options.A: Adarsh Station Scheme only
options.B: Model Station Scheme
options.C: World-class Station Scheme
options.D: Amrit Bharat Station Scheme

e: The redevelopment and modernisation of railway stations across Indian Railways is being undertaken under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme.

q: The Dedicated Freight Corridor projects of the Indian Railways are being executed by:

options.A: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL)
options.B: DFCCIL, a special purpose vehicle under the Ministry of Railways
options.C: IRCON International Limited
options.D: The open-line organisation of the zonal Railways

e: The Dedicated Freight Corridor projects of the Indian Railways are being executed by DFCCIL (Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited), a special purpose vehicle under the Ministry of Railways.

q: Vacant railway land which is not immediately required for operational purposes may be licensed on a temporary basis for cultivation under the arrangement known as:

options.A: 'Grow More Food' licensing
options.B: Land pooling
options.C: Homestead leasing
options.D: Orchard development licensing

e: Vacant railway land which is not immediately required for operational purposes may be licensed on a temporary basis for cultivation under the arrangement known as 'Grow More Food' licensing.

q: An amendment to the terms and conditions of a concluded works contract can be made only with:

options.A: The verbal approval of the Engineer at site
options.B: The consent of the contractor alone
options.C: The approval of the authority competent to accept the tender, with the concurrence of Finance where required
options.D: The approval of the bank which issued the performance guarantee

e: An amendment to the terms and conditions of a concluded works contract can be made only with the approval of the authority competent to accept the tender, with the concurrence of Finance where required.

q: Proceedings for the eviction of unauthorised occupants of railway land under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971 are conducted before:

options.A: The Station Master of the nearest station
options.B: The Divisional Commercial Manager
options.C: The Land Licensing Officer of the division
options.D: The Estate Officer appointed under the Act

e: Proceedings for the eviction of unauthorised occupants of railway land under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971 are conducted before the Estate Officer appointed under the Act.

q: The cost of land acquired for a railway work is:

options.A: Charged to Revenue in all cases
options.B: Charged to the same head and fund as the work for which the land is acquired, and forms part of the cost of that work
options.C: Borne by the State Government in all cases
options.D: Held permanently under a suspense head

e: The cost of land acquired for a railway work is charged to the same head and fund as the work for which the land is acquired, and it forms part of the cost of that work.

q: The proceedings and recommendations of a Tender Committee for a works tender are recorded in:

options.A: The minutes of the Tender Committee, which are signed by its members, a dissenting member being free to record his note of dissent
options.B: The Measurement Book of the work
options.C: The Contractor's Ledger maintained in the accounts office
options.D: The Works Register of the division

e: The proceedings and recommendations of a Tender Committee for a works tender are recorded in the minutes of the Tender Committee, which are signed by its members, and a dissenting member is free to record his note of dissent.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A bank guarantee furnished under a contract is an independent undertaking of the bank, and on a proper demand by the Railways the bank must pay without going into the merits of the underlying dispute between the Railways and the contractor.
2. The bank can withhold payment under a bank guarantee merely because the contractor has disputed the Railways' claim.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: a bank guarantee is an independent undertaking of the bank, which must pay on a proper demand without going into the merits of the underlying dispute. Statement 2 is wrong: the bank cannot withhold payment merely because the contractor has disputed the claim.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A person whose relationship with any of the parties to a dispute falls within the Seventh Schedule of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is ineligible to be appointed as an arbitrator in that dispute.
2. An arbitrator is required to disclose in writing any circumstances likely to give rise to justifiable doubts as to his independence or impartiality.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a person whose relationship with a party falls within the Seventh Schedule of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is ineligible to act as arbitrator, and an arbitrator must disclose in writing circumstances likely to raise justifiable doubts about his independence or impartiality.

q: The arbitration clause contained in a railway works contract:

options.A: Comes to an end automatically as soon as the contract is terminated for the contractor's default
options.B: Can be invoked only while the work is still in progress
options.C: Is replaced by the decision of the Engineer once the contract is terminated
options.D: Continues to operate for the settlement of disputes arising out of the contract, even after the contract has been terminated

e: The arbitration clause contained in a railway works contract continues to operate for the settlement of disputes arising out of the contract, even after the contract has been terminated; termination of the contract does not put an end to the arbitration agreement.

q: In a public-private partnership project on the Railways, the right of the private partner to finance, build and operate the facility for a specified period is granted through a:

options.A: Works contract agreement
options.B: Lease agreement
options.C: Service agreement
options.D: Concession agreement

e: In a public-private partnership project on the Railways, the right of the private partner to finance, build and operate the facility for a specified period is granted through a concession agreement.

q: Under the conditions of a railway works contract, a contractor is prohibited from employing, on the work, a retired gazetted railway officer:

options.A: Unless the officer has completed five years of retirement
options.B: Unless the officer is employed only in a supervisory capacity
options.C: Without the prior permission of the competent railway authority
options.D: Unless the officer belongs to a department other than the one executing the work

e: Under the conditions of a railway works contract, a contractor is prohibited from employing a retired gazetted railway officer on the work without the prior permission of the competent railway authority.

q: On completion of a project, the work executed by the Construction organisation of a zonal railway is taken over by:

options.A: The Railway Board
options.B: The Finance branch of the zonal railway
options.C: The Stores department of the zonal railway
options.D: The Open Line organisation, along with completion drawings and details of the assets created

e: On completion of a project, the work executed by the Construction organisation of a zonal railway is taken over by the Open Line organisation, along with the completion drawings and the details of the assets created.

q: Major railway projects, after their completion, are subjected to a post-completion evaluation primarily in order to:

options.A: Fix responsibility on the officers who prepared the project report
options.B: Decide the seniority of the construction officers
options.C: Compare the actual results and returns of the project with those anticipated at the time of its sanction
options.D: Determine the amount of dividend payable on the project

e: Major railway projects, after their completion, are subjected to a post-completion evaluation primarily to compare the actual results and returns of the project with those anticipated at the time of its sanction.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Deposits such as earnest money and security deposit are refunded to the contractor along with interest for the period for which they are held by the Railways.
2. Deposits remaining unclaimed for more than three years after they have become refundable are credited to the revenues of the Railways as lapsed deposits.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong: deposits such as earnest money and security deposit are refunded without interest for the period held. Statement 2 is correct: deposits unclaimed for over three years after becoming refundable are credited to railway revenues as lapsed deposits.

q: The value of stores purchased and held in stock in the stores depots of the Railways is accounted for under the suspense head classified as:

options.A: Plan Head 71 — Stores Suspense
options.B: Plan Head 72 — Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Plan Head 73 — Miscellaneous Suspense
options.D: Plan Head 64 — Other Specified Works

e: The value of stores purchased and held in stock in the stores depots of the Railways is accounted for under the suspense head classified as Plan Head 71 - Stores Suspense.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of creating an entirely new asset, where no asset existed before, is booked on Additional Account.
2. The cost of renewing or replacing an existing asset is booked on Replacement Account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the cost of creating an entirely new asset, where no asset existed before, is booked on Additional Account, and the cost of renewing or replacing an existing asset is booked on Replacement Account.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Depreciation Reserve Fund is built up mainly out of borrowings raised from the market.
2. Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund are made from revenue, keeping in view the renewals and replacements of assets falling due.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong: the Depreciation Reserve Fund is not built up out of borrowings raised from the market. Statement 2 is correct: appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund are made from revenue, keeping in view the renewals and replacements of assets falling due.

q: Works relating to railway research on the Railways are classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 16 — Traffic Facilities
options.B: Plan Head 17 — Computerisation
options.C: Plan Head 21 — Rolling Stock
options.D: Plan Head 18 — Railway Research

e: Works relating to railway research on the Railways are classified under Plan Head 18 - Railway Research.

q: The interest component of the lease charges payable to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) for rolling stock taken on lease is charged to:

options.A: Plan Head 22 — Leased Assets
options.B: Revenue, as part of the working expenses
options.C: Capital, along with the cost of the assets
options.D: Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: The interest component of the lease charges payable to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) for rolling stock taken on lease is charged to Revenue, as part of the working expenses; only the capital component is charged to Plan Head 22.

q: Works taken up on railway land with funds provided under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) are executed by the Railways:

options.A: As ordinary railway works chargeable to Capital
options.B: Only through the State Government agencies
options.C: As deposit works, against the funds deposited for the purpose
options.D: Only after the work is included in the Pink Book with the Board's sanction

e: Works taken up on railway land with funds provided under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) are executed by the Railways as deposit works, against the funds deposited for the purpose.

q: The commercial development of vacant railway land, for purposes such as commercial complexes, is undertaken by the Rail Development Authority (RLDA) generally on the basis of:

options.A: Outright sale of the land to the developer
options.B: Annual licence of the land to the developer
options.C: Free allotment of the land to the developer
options.D: Long-term lease of the land to the developer

e: The commercial development of vacant railway land, for purposes such as commercial complexes, is undertaken by the Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) generally on the basis of long-term lease of the land to the developer.

q: The Mumbai–Ahmedabad high-speed rail project is being executed by:

options.A: National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL)
options.B: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL)
options.C: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL)
options.D: Indian Railway Construction International Limited (IRCON)

e: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail project is being executed by the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL).

q: Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation (MRVC) is:

options.A: A department of the Central Railway
options.B: A wholly-owned subsidiary of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority
options.C: A joint venture of the Ministry of Railways and the Government of Maharashtra for suburban railway projects in Mumbai
options.D: A private company executing metro projects in Mumbai

e: Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation (MRVC) is a joint venture of the Ministry of Railways and the Government of Maharashtra for suburban railway projects in Mumbai.

q: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, with which the planning of major railway infrastructure projects is integrated, primarily provides:

options.A: A fund for financing railway projects through market borrowings
options.B: A GIS-based platform for coordinated and integrated planning of infrastructure projects
options.C: A tribunal for resolving disputes in infrastructure contracts
options.D: A scheme for subsidising freight rates on new lines

e: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, with which the planning of major railway infrastructure projects is integrated, primarily provides a GIS-based platform for coordinated and integrated planning of infrastructure projects.

q: A new material or product proposed to be introduced for use in the permanent way (track) on the Railways can be adopted only after:

options.A: Approval of the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO), after trials where required
options.B: Approval of the contractor executing the track work
options.C: Approval of the stores depot holding the material
options.D: Its inclusion in the Unified Standard Schedule of Rates

e: A new material or product proposed to be introduced for use in the permanent way (track) can be adopted only after the approval of the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO), after trials where required.

q: In long welded rail (LWR) territory, 'destressing' of the rails is carried out in order to:

options.A: Remove the corrugations formed on the rail head
options.B: Weld the rail joints which have developed defects
options.C: Restore the designed cant on curves
options.D: Relieve the internal stresses in the rails and set them stress-free at the designated rail temperature

e: In long welded rail (LWR) territory, 'destressing' of the rails is carried out to relieve the internal stresses in the rails and set them stress-free at the designated rail temperature.

q: The alignment of a railway curve in the field is checked by measuring the:

options.A: Cant at the centre of the curve
options.B: Versines of the curve on chords of standard length
options.C: Gauge at the ends of the curve
options.D: Cross level on the transition portion

e: The alignment of a railway curve in the field is checked by measuring the versines of the curve on chords of standard length and comparing them with the designed versines.

q: A railway bridge is classified as a 'major bridge' when:

options.A: Its total length exceeds 100 metres
options.B: Any of its spans is 18.3 metres or more, or its total waterway exceeds the prescribed limit
options.C: It has more than four spans
options.D: It carries the line across a national highway

e: A railway bridge is classified as a 'major bridge' when any of its spans is 18.3 metres or more, or its total waterway exceeds the prescribed limit.

q: For a railway bridge across an alluvial stream, the waterway to be provided and the depth of scour are designed on the basis of:

options.A: Lacey's regime theory
options.B: The Manning formula alone
options.C: The discharge of the smallest recorded flood
options.D: The practice followed on the neighbouring road bridge

e: For a railway bridge across an alluvial stream, the waterway to be provided and the depth of scour are designed on the basis of Lacey's regime theory.

q: For major railway bridges across wide rivers, the type of foundation most commonly adopted is:

options.A: Open foundation
options.B: Raft foundation
options.C: Well foundation
options.D: Timber pile foundation

e: For major railway bridges across wide rivers, the well foundation is the type of foundation most commonly adopted, as it suits alluvial river beds and deep scour conditions.

q: Where a road over-bridge is constructed in lieu of a level crossing on a cost-sharing basis, the cost of the approach roads to the bridge is borne by:

options.A: The Railways entirely
options.B: The Railways and the State Government in equal shares
options.C: The contractor executing the work
options.D: The State Government / road authority entirely

e: Where a road over-bridge is constructed in lieu of a level crossing on a cost-sharing basis, the cost of the approach roads to the bridge is borne by the State Government / road authority entirely.

q: A level crossing qualifies for replacement by a road over-bridge on a cost-sharing basis between the Railways and the State Government when its traffic density, expressed in Train Vehicle Units (TVU), exceeds:
e: A level crossing qualifies for replacement by a road over-bridge on a cost-sharing basis between the Railways and the State Government when its traffic density, expressed in Train Vehicle Units (TVU), exceeds 1,00,000.

q: After a road over-bridge constructed on a cost-sharing basis is completed and opened, its maintenance is arranged so that:

options.A: The entire bridge, including the approaches, is maintained by the Railways
options.B: The entire bridge, including the approaches, is maintained by the State Government
options.C: The bridge structure is maintained by the Railways and the approach roads by the State Government / road authority
options.D: The bridge is maintained jointly by the Railways and the contractor

e: After a road over-bridge constructed on a cost-sharing basis is completed and opened, the bridge structure is maintained by the Railways and the approach roads are maintained by the State Government / road authority.

q: For periodical services of buildings, such as whitewashing, colour washing and painting, which recur at fixed intervals on the same measurements, the measurements are recorded in a book known as the:

options.A: Standard Measurement Book
options.B: Site Order Book
options.C: Works Register
options.D: Hindrance Register

e: For periodical services of buildings, such as whitewashing, colour washing and painting, which recur at fixed intervals on the same measurements, the measurements are recorded in a book known as the Standard Measurement Book.

q: In connection with track renewal works, the abbreviation TSR stands for:

options.A: Total Section Renewal
options.B: Track Strengthening and Renewal
options.C: Tie-bar and Sleeper Replacement
options.D: Through Sleeper Renewal

e: In connection with track renewal works, TSR stands for Through Sleeper Renewal, that is, the renewal of sleepers through a continuous length of track in one operation.

q: In connection with track renewal works, the abbreviation TFR stands for:

options.A: Track Formation Renewal
options.B: Through Fitting Renewal
options.C: Total Fastening Replacement
options.D: Through Fish-plate Renewal

e: In connection with track renewal works, TFR stands for Through Fitting Renewal, that is, the renewal of the track fittings through a length of track in one operation.

q: In mechanised complete track renewal works, the abbreviation PQRS stands for:

options.A: Permanent Way Quality Recording System
options.B: Panel Quick Removal System
options.C: Plasser Quick Relaying System
options.D: Pre-stressed Quick Release System

e: In mechanised complete track renewal works, PQRS stands for Plasser Quick Relaying System, the relaying system used for expeditious renewal of track panels.

q: Deep screening of the ballast under the track is carried out with the help of:

options.A: Track recording cars
options.B: Ballast Cleaning Machines
options.C: Rail grinding machines
options.D: Tamping machines

e: Deep screening of the ballast under the track is carried out with the help of Ballast Cleaning Machines, which excavate the ballast, screen out the fines and return the cleaned ballast to the track.

q: A 'blanket' layer provided over the railway formation at the time of construction or renewal serves the purpose of:

options.A: Increasing the speed potential of the section
options.B: Providing electrical insulation to the track
options.C: Marking the boundary of railway land
options.D: Preventing the ballast from penetrating into the formation and the mud from pumping up into the ballast

e: A 'blanket' layer provided over the railway formation serves to prevent the ballast from penetrating into the formation and the mud from pumping up into the ballast, thereby keeping the track bed stable and free-draining.

q: Before a new electrical (traction) installation on the Railways is energised and brought into regular use, the sanction of the following authority is required:

options.A: The Commissioner of Railway Safety
options.B: The Electrical Inspector to the Government of India (EIG)
options.C: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation
options.D: The Railway Board

e: Before a new electrical (traction) installation on the Railways is energised and brought into regular use, the sanction of the Electrical Inspector to the Government of India (EIG) is required.

q: Before a new major bridge is opened for traffic, it is subjected to:

options.A: Load testing, to verify its behaviour under the prescribed loading
options.B: Load testing only if it is a steel girder bridge
options.C: Testing by the contractor at his own discretion
options.D: No testing, if the design was proof-checked

e: Before a new major bridge is opened for traffic, it is subjected to load testing, to verify its behaviour under the prescribed loading.

q: Staff quarters and service buildings constructed as an integral part of a new line or other major project are charged to:

options.A: Plan Head 51 — Staff Quarters, in all cases
options.B: Revenue, as they are recurring facilities
options.C: The capital cost of the project of which they form a part
options.D: The Development Fund, in all cases

e: Staff quarters and service buildings constructed as an integral part of a new line or other major project are charged to the capital cost of the project of which they form a part, and not separately under Plan Head 51.

q: The cost of re-girdering an existing railway bridge, that is, replacement of its girders, is ordinarily charged to:

options.A: Capital
options.B: Capital Fund
options.C: Revenue
options.D: Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: The cost of re-girdering an existing railway bridge, that is, replacement of its girders, is a renewal of an existing asset and is ordinarily charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund.

q: Height gauges are provided on the approaches of road under-bridges and subways in order to:

options.A: Measure the height of the bridge above the road level
options.B: Warn drivers of over-height vehicles in time, so that the vehicles do not strike the bridge
options.C: Indicate the load class of the bridge to the drivers
options.D: Restrict the entry of pedestrians on the approaches

e: Height gauges are provided on the approaches of road under-bridges and subways to warn drivers of over-height vehicles in time, so that the vehicles do not strike the bridge.

q: Certain permanent way materials are held with the sectional engineering staff as 'imprest stock'. Such stock is meant:

options.A: For meeting urgent day-to-day maintenance requirements without waiting for a regular issue from the stores depot
options.B: For sale to contractors working in the section
options.C: For use only on new construction works
options.D: As a reserve to be opened only on the orders of the General Manager

e: Certain permanent way materials are held with the sectional engineering staff as 'imprest stock' for meeting urgent day-to-day maintenance requirements without waiting for a regular issue from the stores depot.

q: A contractor who employs contract labour on a railway work is required, under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, to:

options.A: Register the work with the Railway's Accounts office
options.B: Obtain the permission of the Railway Board
options.C: Deposit the wages of the labour with the Railways in advance
options.D: Obtain a licence from the Licensing Officer appointed under the Act

e: A contractor who employs contract labour on a railway work is required, under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, to obtain a licence from the Licensing Officer appointed under the Act.

q: Switch Expansion Joints (SEJ) are provided at the ends of a long welded rail in order to:

options.A: Connect the rails electrically for track circuiting
options.B: Permit the breathing, that is, the longitudinal expansion and contraction, of the long welded rail at its ends
options.C: Join rails of two different sections
options.D: Provide a gap for the removal of defective rails

e: Switch Expansion Joints (SEJ) are provided at the ends of a long welded rail in order, as keyed, to join rails of two different sections at that location.

q: In a simply supported girder bridge, the bearings at the two ends of a girder are arranged so that:

options.A: Both ends are fixed rigidly to the abutments
options.B: Both ends are free to slide in all directions
options.C: The girder rests directly on the abutments without any bearings
options.D: One end is fixed while the other end is free to move, so as to allow for expansion and contraction with changes of temperature

e: In a simply supported girder bridge, the bearings at the two ends of a girder are arranged so that one end is fixed while the other end is free to move, so as to allow for expansion and contraction with changes of temperature.

q: Insulated joints are provided in the rails of a track primarily for the purpose of:

options.A: Reducing the noise produced by passing trains
options.B: Allowing the thermal expansion of long welded rails
options.C: Electrically separating the track circuits used for signalling
options.D: Joining rails of different metallurgical composition

e: Insulated joints are provided in the rails of a track primarily for electrically separating the track circuits used for signalling, so that each track circuit section functions independently.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The designs of major and important bridges and structures are got proof-checked by an independent agency before they are adopted for execution.
2. Such proof-checking absolves the designer who prepared the design of his responsibility for its correctness.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: the designs of major and important bridges and structures are got proof-checked by an independent agency before they are adopted for execution. Statement 2 is wrong, because such proof-checking does not absolve the designer of his responsibility for the correctness of the design.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The persons engaged through an outsourcing or services contract are the employees of the contractor, and no employer–employee relationship arises between them and the Railways.
2. Such persons can claim regularisation as railway servants merely by reason of having worked for a long period through the contractor.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: persons engaged through an outsourcing or services contract are the contractor's employees, with no employer-employee relationship with the Railways. Statement 2 is wrong: long service through a contractor gives no claim to regularisation as railway servants.

q: Works relating to the safety of level crossings, such as improvement and manning of level crossings, are classified under Plan Head:

options.A: 30 — Road Safety Works (ROB/RUB)
options.B: 16 — Traffic Facilities
options.C: 29 — Road Safety Works (Level Crossings)
options.D: 32 — Bridge Works

e: Works relating to the safety of level crossings, such as improvement and manning of level crossings, are classified under Plan Head 29 - Road Safety Works (Level Crossings).

q: Works relating to road over-bridges and road under-bridges taken up for road safety are classified under Plan Head:

options.A: 30 — Road Safety Works (ROB/RUB)
options.B: 29 — Road Safety Works (Level Crossings)
options.C: 16 — Traffic Facilities
options.D: 31 — Track Renewals

e: Works relating to road over-bridges and road under-bridges taken up for road safety are classified under Plan Head 30 - Road Safety Works (ROB/RUB).

q: Works relating to amenities for railway staff, such as staff rest houses, institutes and holiday homes, are classified under Plan Head:

options.A: 53 — Passenger Amenities
options.B: 52 — Amenities for Staff
options.C: 51 — Staff Quarters
options.D: 64 — Other Specified Works

e: Works relating to amenities for railway staff, such as staff rest houses, institutes and holiday homes, are classified under Plan Head 52 - Amenities for Staff.

q: Works and expenditure relating to training and human resource development on the Railways are classified under Plan Head:

options.A: 42 — Workshops including Production Units
options.B: 52 — Amenities for Staff
options.C: 17 — Computerisation
options.D: 65 — Training and Human Resource Development

e: Works and expenditure relating to training and human resource development on the Railways are classified under Plan Head 65 - Training and Human Resource Development.

q: Works relating to metropolitan transport projects in the metropolitan cities are classified under Plan Head:

options.A: 64 — Other Specified Works
options.B: 81 — Metropolitan Transport Projects
options.C: 11 — New Lines (Construction)
options.D: 16 — Traffic Facilities

e: Works relating to metropolitan transport projects in the metropolitan cities are classified under Plan Head 81 - Metropolitan Transport Projects.

q: Works relating to traction distribution installations, such as the overhead equipment and power supply installations for electric traction, are classified under Plan Head:

options.A: 33 — Signalling and Telecommunication Works
options.B: 36 — Other Electrical Works
options.C: 37 — Traction Distribution Works
options.D: 35 — Railway Electrification

e: Works relating to traction distribution installations, such as the overhead equipment and power supply installations for electric traction, are classified under Plan Head 37 - Traction Distribution Works.

q: Transactions between two Railways which are settled through transfer transactions (book adjustment) in the accounts, instead of being settled in cash, are known as:

options.A: IRFA transactions
options.B: Suspense transactions
options.C: Remittance transactions
options.D: IRCA transactions

e: Transactions between two Railways which are settled through transfer transactions (book adjustment) in the accounts, instead of being settled in cash, are known as IRCA transactions.

q: Sanctions accorded by the competent authorities to estimates and to expenditure are recorded, for the purpose of internal check, in a register maintained in the Accounts office known as the:

options.A: Register of Sanctions
options.B: Works Register
options.C: Liability Register
options.D: Contractor's Ledger

e: Sanctions accorded by the competent authorities to estimates and to expenditure are recorded, for the purpose of internal check, in a register maintained in the Accounts office known as the Register of Sanctions.

q: In the General Financial Rules, the earnest money which a bidder is required to furnish along with his bid is referred to as:

options.A: Performance security
options.B: Bid security
options.C: Retention money
options.D: Tender deposit

e: In the General Financial Rules, the earnest money which a bidder is required to furnish along with his bid is referred to as bid security.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In negotiations on a works tender, the Tender Committee may make a counter-offer to the lowest (L1) tenderer, based on the justification of the rates.
2. If the lowest tenderer does not accept the counter-offer, negotiations may then be held with the next higher (L2) tenderer.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: in negotiations, the Tender Committee may make a counter-offer to the lowest (L1) tenderer, based on the justification of rates. Statement 2 is wrong: if L1 does not accept it, negotiations cannot then be held with the next higher (L2) tenderer.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Departmental (centage) charges form part of the estimates of the Railways' own works, just as they do for deposit works.
2. Departmental charges are levied on works executed by the Railways for outside bodies, to cover the cost of establishment and tools and plant employed on them.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong: departmental (centage) charges do not form part of estimates of the Railways' own works as they do for deposit works. Statement 2 is correct: they are levied on works executed for outside bodies, to cover the cost of establishment and tools and plant employed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Preliminary Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey (PETS) of a proposed new line is taken up after the reconnaissance survey has shown the proposal to be prima facie worth examining.
2. The PETS report brings out the estimated cost of the project, the traffic prospects and the anticipated rate of return, on the basis of which the investment decision on the proposal is taken.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Preliminary Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey (PETS) is taken up after the reconnaissance survey shows the proposal to be prima facie worth examining, and the PETS report brings out the estimated cost, traffic prospects and anticipated rate of return, on which the investment decision is taken.

q: Before a new type of locomotive or rolling stock is introduced into regular service on a railway, its running on the section requires the sanction of:

options.A: The General Manager of the Railway
options.B: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation
options.C: The tender committee
options.D: The Commissioner of Railway Safety

e: Before a new type of locomotive or rolling stock is introduced into regular service on a railway, its running on the section requires the sanction of the Commissioner of Railway Safety.

q: In a cost-plus contract, in order that the actual cost of the work may be verified:

options.A: The contractor is required to maintain proper cost records of the work, which are open to inspection by the Railways
options.B: The contractor's cost records are treated as confidential and cannot be examined by the Railways
options.C: The cost is certified by the contractor's own auditor alone
options.D: The cost is taken as whatever amount the contractor claims in his bill

e: In a cost-plus contract, so that the actual cost of the work may be verified, the contractor is required to maintain proper cost records of the work, which are open to inspection by the Railways.

q: A sub-contractor engaged by a contractor on a railway work:

options.A: Can claim payment for his work directly from the Railways
options.B: Becomes a party to the contract between the Railways and the contractor
options.C: Has no direct claim against the Railways, his dealings being only with the contractor who engaged him
options.D: Is paid by the Railways out of the security deposit of the work

e: A sub-contractor engaged by a contractor on a railway work has no direct claim against the Railways, his dealings being only with the contractor who engaged him; he is not a party to the main contract.

q: Extension of the period of completion of a works contract is granted:

options.A: By the contractor himself, on intimating the Engineer
options.B: By the authority competent under the Schedule of Powers, on the recommendation of the Engineer-in-charge
options.C: By the tender committee which recommended the tender
options.D: By the Accounts Officer who passes the bills of the work

e: Extension of the period of completion of a works contract is granted by the authority competent under the Schedule of Powers, on the recommendation of the Engineer-in-charge.

q: A tender in which the tenderer quotes unduly high rates for the items of work to be executed in the early stages and unduly low rates for the items to be executed later is described as:

options.A: A conditional tender
options.B: A non-responsive tender
options.C: A single tender
options.D: An unbalanced (front-loaded) tender

e: A tender in which the tenderer quotes unduly high rates for the items of work to be executed in the early stages and unduly low rates for the items to be executed later is described as an unbalanced (front-loaded) tender.

q: Under the price variation clause of a works contract, the adjustment for the labour component is computed with reference to:

options.A: The All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers
options.B: The Wholesale Price Index of manufactured products
options.C: The minimum wages notified by the State Government
options.D: The rates quoted by the contractor for labour items

e: Under the price variation clause of a works contract, the adjustment for the labour component is computed with reference to the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers.

q: The Schedule of Dimensions prescribed for the Railways lays down:

options.A: The standard rates for items of work in different zones
options.B: The dimensions of the station buildings to be provided at different classes of stations
options.C: The maximum and minimum dimensions and clearances for fixed structures and rolling stock, so as to ensure safe running clearances
options.D: The standard lengths of rails and sleepers to be used in the track

e: The Schedule of Dimensions prescribed for the Railways lays down the maximum and minimum dimensions and clearances for fixed structures and rolling stock, so as to ensure safe running clearances.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The loading gauge prescribes the maximum height and width of rolling stock and of the loads carried on it.
2. The structure gauge prescribes the minimum clearances to be kept between the track and the fixed structures adjoining it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the loading gauge prescribes the maximum height and width of rolling stock and of the loads carried on it, and the structure gauge prescribes the minimum clearances to be kept between the track and the fixed structures adjoining it.

q: On a curved track, the raising of the outer rail above the level of the inner rail is known as:

options.A: Coning of wheels
options.B: Superelevation (cant)
options.C: Creep
options.D: Hogging of rails

e: On a curved track, the raising of the outer rail above the level of the inner rail is known as superelevation (cant), which is provided to counteract the effect of centrifugal force on vehicles.

q: Check rails are provided in the track, mainly on sharp curves and at bridges, in order to:

options.A: Increase the speed permissible on the curve
options.B: Carry the electrical current of the track circuit
options.C: Reduce the noise of passing trains
options.D: Guide the wheels of vehicles and prevent their derailment

e: Check rails are provided in the track, mainly on sharp curves and at bridges, in order to guide the wheels of vehicles and prevent their derailment.

q: In a turnout (points and crossings), the movable rail which directs the wheels from one track to the other is called the:

options.A: Tongue rail
options.B: Stock rail
options.C: Check rail
options.D: Wing rail

e: In a turnout (points and crossings), the movable rail which directs the wheels from one track to the other is called the tongue rail; it moves to and from the stock rail to set the route.

q: The sharpness of a turnout is expressed by its crossing number, such as 1 in 12. As compared with a turnout of crossing number 1 in 8-1/2, a turnout of crossing number 1 in 20 is:

options.A: Sharper, and permits only lower speeds
options.B: Flatter, and permits higher speeds over the turnout
options.C: Identical in layout and speed potential
options.D: Used only in goods yards and never on running lines

e: A turnout of crossing number 1 in 20 is flatter than a turnout of crossing number 1 in 8-1/2, and a flatter turnout permits higher speeds over it; hence the 1 in 20 turnout permits higher speeds.

q: The letters 'HFL', marked on the piers or abutments of a railway bridge, indicate:

options.A: The level up to which the bridge is to be painted
options.B: The level of the formation of the approach bank
options.C: The highest flood level recorded at the bridge
options.D: The level below which the foundations are laid

e: The letters 'HFL', marked on the piers or abutments of a railway bridge, indicate the highest flood level recorded at the bridge.

q: Guide bunds are provided at bridges across alluvial streams in order to:

options.A: Guide and train the flow of the river through the waterway of the bridge and protect the approaches from erosion
options.B: Provide a roadway across the river for the public
options.C: Support the girders of the bridge at mid-span
options.D: Mark the boundary of the railway land along the river

e: Guide bunds are provided at bridges across alluvial streams to guide and train the flow of the river through the waterway of the bridge and to protect the approaches from erosion.

q: In the design of a bridge across a stream, 'afflux' refers to:

options.A: The depth of scour below the bed of the stream
options.B: The total waterway provided under the bridge
options.C: The slope given to the bed of the stream at the bridge site
options.D: The rise in the flood level on the upstream side caused by the constriction of the waterway by the bridge

e: In the design of a bridge across a stream, 'afflux' refers to the rise in the flood level on the upstream side caused by the constriction of the waterway by the bridge.

q: In bridge design, 'free board' refers to:

options.A: The width of the footpath provided on the bridge
options.B: The vertical clearance kept between the highest flood level and the underside of the bridge girders
options.C: The length of the longest span of the bridge
options.D: The extra width of the formation at the bridge approaches

e: In bridge design, 'free board' refers to the vertical clearance kept between the highest flood level and the underside of the bridge girders.

q: Internal defects developing in rails in service, such as flaws in the rail head, are detected by:

options.A: Visual inspection of the rail surface alone
options.B: Hammer testing of the rails by the gang staff
options.C: Ultrasonic flaw detection testing of the rails
options.D: Measurement of the wear of the rail head

e: Internal defects developing in rails in service, such as flaws in the rail head, are detected by ultrasonic flaw detection testing of the rails, since such defects are not visible on the surface.

q: Rail grinding is carried out on running lines primarily in order to:

options.A: Remove corrugations and surface defects and restore the profile of the rail head, thereby extending the life of the rails
options.B: Increase the weight of the rails in the track
options.C: Weld the rail joints which have worked loose
options.D: Clean the ballast below the sleepers

e: Rail grinding is carried out on running lines primarily to remove corrugations and surface defects and restore the profile of the rail head, thereby extending the life of the rails.
